# Requirements: screw

**Defined:** 2026-10-05
**Core Value:** A bolt and a nut generated by this tool actually thread together when printed, and every number it prints is one someone can cut metal to — computed honestly from explicit millimetres or a cited ISO row, or reported as a warning and no number.

Every requirement below is phrased as something a user can observe or a test can check. Where a value is not yet measured (clearance default, build timeout, printability threshold) the requirement names the measurement that sets it; it never names a number from a blog or from memory (L02). Sources: the owner's brief and decisions of 2026-10-05 (PROJECT.md § Key Decisions), `.planning/research/` (STACK, FEATURES, ARCHITECTURE, PITFALLS, SUMMARY).

## v1 Requirements

Requirements for the first release: the mating-pair cut (infra port, thread spike, hex bolt, hex nut, proven pair). Each maps to a roadmap phase.

### Thread Geometry

- [x] **THRD-01**: Every threaded part carries a real helical ISO metric coarse-pitch thread (ISO 68-1:2023 profile; basic vs design profile pinned by the thread spike's decision entry after the standard is read). There is no cosmetic or unthreaded option in v1.
- [x] **THRD-02**: User can choose a left-hand thread via a boolean `left_hand` field (default right-hand); a left-hand pair is proven by the same checks as a right-hand pair. *(Phase 3 ships the right- and left-hand solid; the second clause, a left-hand pair proven like a right-hand pair, is Phase 5 PAIR-03 — owner ruling 2026-10-11.)*
- [x] **THRD-03**: User sets `thread_length` on a bolt as explicit millimetres; the ISO 4017 preset fills it with the full length, the ISO 4014 preset fills `b` from the table by length band; the user may edit it afterwards.
- [x] **THRD-04**: Every thread build is gated by a postcondition — valid shape, exactly one solid, volume within a stated tolerance of the closed-form value (sign included) — and a failed gate is a `BuildError` naming what failed, never a cached or served solid. `isValid()` alone is never the gate; the gate has a positive-control test fed a known-bad build.
- [x] **THRD-05**: Nut thread and bolt tip carry lead-in chamfers and the bolt an under-head fillet (bolt ends per ISO 4753 — clause UNVERIFIED until the standard is read; L14, 2026-10-20: read as GOST 12414-94, the ISO 4753:1983 text) so a printed pair can start. *(Evidence, Phase 5: `tests/test_solid.py::test_every_size_of_both_standards_meshes_watertight_at_preview` and `tests/test_end_oracles.py` for the bolt ends, `tests/test_nut.py::test_every_iso_4032_nut_meshes_watertight_at_preview` for the nut's; the end models, each labelled cited or stated model, in decision log L15.)*

### Mating Pair

- [x] **PAIR-01**: User sets one `clearance` field, on the nut, in radial millimetres; a positive value moves the nut's thread surfaces away from the axis (larger hole, material removed from the nut). The bolt is built to nominal. The info panel shows both the radial and the diametral value. *(Evidence, Phase 5: `tests/test_nut.py::test_a_positive_clearance_moves_the_nut_thread_away_from_the_axis_on_both_hands`; the radial and diametral rows in `tests/test_calc.py::test_the_nut_pair_rows_are_the_eight_keys_in_the_fixed_order`.)*
- [x] **PAIR-02**: The default `clearance` is set once, before the first release, from a recorded FDM printed test (M6–M12 matrix, owner checkpoint) and cited in the decision log; it is never taken from a forum or vendor figure. Until the test is recorded, no default ships. *(Evidence, Phase 6: decision log L17, 0.15 mm read by `bench.print_rules.default_from` from run `06-print-run-1` (record sha256 `f76753ded41726daec0a11ec4c5eabc5f4d2afb094cbe258d5e9d915aa6db725`) and accepted as permanent by the owner on 2026-10-23; `tests/test_print_rules.py::test_the_shipped_clearance_default_is_the_one_run_1_reads`.)*
- [x] **PAIR-03**: A kernel-level interference check proves a bolt/nut pair at the chosen clearance and returns `proven | violated | inconclusive` with its control: a half-pitch axial offset of the same pair must collide, or the verdict is `inconclusive`, never `proven`. Clearance ≤ 0 is `inconclusive` by definition. *(Evidence, Phase 5: `tests/test_pair.py::test_the_verify_cell_is_proven_as_pre_registered` and the kernel-free rule tests with positive controls in the same file; 240 of 240 grid cells equal their pre-registered verdict, `bench/RESULTS.md` "Pair tier (Phase 5, D-07)"; decision log L15.)*
- [x] **PAIR-04**: The pair check is exposed as a function in the solid package, a `screw pair` CLI subcommand and a slow-tier test (one size in `make verify`, the full grid in a CI job). It is not an API endpoint; the API and UI show closed-form flank gaps instead. *(Evidence, Phase 5: `tests/test_cli_pair.py` (exit codes 0, 1, 2), `tests/test_import_boundaries.py` and the contract "The serving process and its workers never import the pair proof", `.github/workflows/pair.yml` and `make pair`. The first ubuntu run of the full grid is not yet recorded: `docs/tech_debt/active/2026-10-14-first-pair-yml-dispatch.md`.)*
- [x] **PAIR-05**: A bolt and nut from this tool, printed on an FDM printer at the chosen clearance, thread together by hand — the owner's manual acceptance for the release; a kernel `proven` is necessary, not sufficient. *(Evidence, Phase 6: `bench/RESULTS.md` "Acceptance pair (Phase 6, D-16)". The kernel read `proven` for the M8 pair at the shipped 0.15 mm default; the owner's page downloads (ISO 4017 M8 x 16 bolt, its Matching nut link, clearance left at the default) equal the pre-registered `manifest-acceptance.tsv` in name, bytes and sha256 (bolt `30f2fca0...5814`, nut `4c09af10...6324`); the owner printed that fresh pair on 2026-10-23 at 21:53 with the protocol's one profile and recorded `pass`, threading by hand under D-05. Matrix and run-2 samples are excluded, D-16.)*

### Fastener Types

- [x] **TYPE-01**: User can generate a hex head bolt per ISO 4014:2022 (partial thread): across-flats `s`, across-corners `e`, head height `k`, bearing face `dw`, thread length `b` by length band, unthreaded shank `ls`/grip `lg`, product grade A/B boundary (A for d ≤ M24 and l ≤ 10d or 150 mm). The chamfered point and the under-head fillet are THRD-05's (Phase 5, ISO 4753).
- [x] **TYPE-02**: User can generate a hex head screw per ISO 4017:2022 (threaded to the head), lengths to the standard's 200 mm cap.
- [x] **TYPE-03**: User can generate a hex nut per ISO 4032:2023 (style 1): `s`, `e`, height `m`, wrench height `mw`, `dw`, chamfers on both faces; M5–M20 from the normative tables, M2–M4 from informative Annex A labelled "informative / historical" in the preset and on the info panel. Amended 2026-10-20 (L14): the rows are read from GOST ISO 4032-2014 (ISO 4032:2012), which has no Annex A, so by the owner's ruling every size M2–M20 it prints (Table 1 and Table 2; no M7) ships as a normative row citing its table and none is labelled informative. *(Evidence, Phase 5: the 14 GOST ISO 4032-2014 rows and their relation tests in `tests/test_tables.py`, the frozen defaults pinned to the M6 row in `tests/test_params.py`, the catalogue and exact match in `tests/test_presets.py` and `tests/test_calc.py`; no row is labelled informative by the owner's 2026-10-20 ruling, `05-OWNER-READS.md`.)*
- [x] **TYPE-04**: For any generated bolt the user can get the matching nut, and vice versa, derived from the same `d`, pitch, hand and clearance. *(Evidence, Phase 5: `tests/test_calc.py::test_following_a_bolts_counterpart_gives_the_nut_row_of_its_size`, `test_following_a_nuts_counterpart_gives_a_bolt_with_the_nuts_d_pitch_and_hand` and `tests/test_parity.py::test_the_cli_and_the_api_print_the_same_counterpart`.)*

### ISO Tables and Presets

- [x] **TABL-01**: User picks standard + size + length from the valid combinations ("M6 × 20, ISO 4017"); the preset fills the explicit mm fields; the shareable URL carries mm fields only, the preset id is metadata and never the source of truth.
- [x] **TABL-02**: Every table row cites standard, edition, table and column in a required typed `Source` field; a row without a citation does not type-check.
- [x] **TABL-03**: Every table row has one verification test asserting the standard's invariants for that row (pure data test; no kernel build per row).
- [x] **TABL-04**: A table row ships only against a purchased copy of its standard (v1: ISO 4014:2022, 4017:2022, 4032:2023, 262:2023, 724:2023, 965-2:2024; ISO 4753 (Phase 5)); rows entered from previews are marked UNVERIFIED and the gate refuses an UNVERIFIED row in a release build. Amended 2026-10-20 (L14): for Phase 5, for the documents L14 maps, the free GOST text stands in for the purchased ISO copy (GOST ISO 4032-2014, GOST 24705-2004, GOST 16093-2004, GOST 12414-94, and GOST ISO 4014-2014 where L14's open question selects it), and each row cites the GOST designation and the ISO edition it adopts; buying the ISO texts is debt.
- [x] **TABL-05**: Sizes M2–M20 per ISO 262:2023 — first choice M2, M2.5, M3, M4, M5, M6, M8, M10, M12, M16, M20; second choice M3.5, M7, M14, M18 shown in brackets as the standards do — coarse pitch only.
- [x] **TABL-06**: The UI shows a preset-match badge: "matches ISO 4017 M6 × 20" while the mm fields equal the row, "custom, based on ISO 4017 M6 × 20" once any field is edited.
- [x] **TABL-07**: The designation line shows the ISO designation without a property class (printed plastic has none).

### Info Panel

- [x] **INFO-01**: The info panel shows, from the pure-maths module without touching the kernel: head (`s` nominal/max/min, across-corners geometric and `e,min` labelled separately, `k`, `dw,min`, wrench size), shank/thread (`l`, `b`, `ls`, `lg`, `d`, `P`, `d2`, `D1`, thread depth), nut (`s`, `e`, `m`, `mw`, `dw`, `D1`, `D2`), pair (clearance radial and diametral, resulting nut diameters, engagement in turns). *(Evidence, Phase 5: `tests/test_calc.py` (the nut's thread rows, `test_the_nut_pair_rows_are_the_eight_keys_in_the_fixed_order`, the nut rows of an exact row) and `tests/test_thread_maths.py` for the closed forms.)*
- [x] **INFO-02**: 6g (bolt) and 6H (nut) min/max limits from ISO 965-2:2024 are shown with the explicit label "limits for a bought part; this model is nominal and not toleranced". Amended 2026-10-20 (L14): the limits are derived from the GOST 24705-2004 basic diameters plus the GOST 16093-2004 printed deviations and tolerances, and each row says derived and names both. *(Evidence, Phase 5: `tests/test_calc.py::test_the_limits_heading_is_the_ascii_text_of_info_02`, `test_every_iso_262_size_shows_its_own_stored_limits_on_both_kinds`, `tests/test_parity.py::test_the_limits_heading_is_the_same_ascii_string_on_the_cli_and_the_api` and the derived limits in `tests/test_tables.py`.)*
- [x] **INFO-03**: Every number on the panel is traceable to an explicit mm field or to a cited row with a test; a value that cannot be computed honestly is a warning and no number. Any volume shown comes from the closed form, never from the kernel's default `Volume()`.
- [x] **INFO-04**: Sizes and pitches below the printable threshold get a cap-and-warn printability warning citing its source; the threshold is a constant set from the owner's printed test, not from vendor guides. *(Evidence, Phase 6: decision log L18, M4 (`D_MIN_MM` 4.0, `P_MIN_MM` 0.7) read by `bench.print_rules.threshold_from` from run `06-print-run-2` (record sha256 `6c2d924006db1ccca860b665fdc2cbcd3c84137b0edefb417e6c31aab9dd923e`), the owner's earlier prints accepted under R10, so weaker evidence than the pre-registered run; `tests/test_print_rules.py::test_the_printability_threshold_is_the_one_run_2_reads`, the printability tests in `tests/test_calc.py` and `tests/test_parity.py`. It warns on bolts and nuts and never caps or refuses (D-13): nothing can be trimmed without changing a d or pitch the user set (L02).)*
- [x] **INFO-05**: Where the wrench size differs from the withdrawn DIN equivalent (M10, M12 and M14 only, D-20) the panel shows the ISO value with a one-line note.

### Front Ends

- [x] **FRNT-01**: One frozen Pydantic model per fastener kind over a shared base, registered by `kind`; `kind` is the URL path segment, the CLI subcommand and the UI hash. A field that does not belong to the kind is a `422` naming it, never silently ignored.
- [x] **FRNT-02**: The web UI is generated from `/api/schema`: form, live 3D preview, info panel, shareable URL carrying the full parameter set with defaults omitted (L02).
- [x] **FRNT-03**: The HTTP API serves info, STL and STEP, schema and health per kind; admission control (bounded queue, `503` + `Retry-After`) lives in the web layer only.
- [x] **FRNT-04**: The CLI offers `screw serve | info | export | pair` with flags generated from the model; it never imports the web layer.
- [x] **FRNT-05**: Each kind ships on UI, API and CLI in the same change, with parity proven model-driven (one test over the registry), not by hand.
- [x] **FRNT-06**: STL and STEP come from the same modelled-thread solid. The STL chord deviation is explicit, recorded and chosen against the clearance so the mesh never consumes it (`ControlSurfaceDeflection` stays on for downloads); the preview may use a coarser mesh, the numbers may not. *(Evidence, Phase 5: `bench/RESULTS.md` "Mesh deviation (Phase 5, D-21)", worst 0.0161 mm against the 0.025 mm bound; `tests/test_mesh.py` pins `ControlSurfaceDeflection` on and the fine preset; decision log L15; the preview STL's name, `tests/test_parity.py::test_the_api_header_and_the_cli_name_a_download_alike`.)*

### Operability

- [x] **OPER-01**: CAD builds run in worker processes off the event loop with a per-build timeout measured by the thread spike over the whole allowed grid (every size, every standard length, including lengths where `L/P` is an integer), recorded as a constant with its measurement cited.
- [x] **OPER-02**: Memory ceiling, gzip level, worker count and bytes-cache budget are re-swept for threaded parts on linux/amd64 before any is set; none of spur's figures is carried.
- [ ] **OPER-03**: Every allowed configuration builds inside the timeout; a configuration that cannot is capped and warned or refused with a `422`, never silently shortened.

### Infrastructure Port

- [x] **INFR-01**: spur's runtime is ported per L07 — `pool`, `records`, `app`, `cli`, `build_errors` retyped over screw's models; the schema-driven form, viewer and vendored three.js; `scripts/pr_land.py`, `scripts/skip_tokens.py`, the commit-msg hook and the `main` ruleset; `docker/` and compose; the coverage floor; the bench harness — with a walking-skeleton kind so the retyping has a target and parity is tested from the first phase.
- [x] **INFR-02**: The module graph is enforced by import-linter: the four inherited contracts plus the new ones — `params` and `calc` never import `tables` or the kernel; `tables` is a leaf; `solid` is the only doorway to `cadquery`/`OCP`; `cli` never imports the web layer; `app` never imports the kernel by any path.
- [x] **INFR-03**: The thread spike is pre-registered (method, predictions, escape clause committed before the first run), run behind a quiet-host gate with load readings labelled by when they were taken, and its result is a decision entry — construction chosen, volume estimator chosen, turn cap per size — before any thread field exists.

## v2 Requirements

Deferred to the second release. Tracked but not in the current roadmap.

### Fastener Types

- **TYP2-01**: Socket head cap screw per ISO 4762:2004 (grade A): cylindrical head, hex socket, `b = 2d + 12` for M1.6–M12 (rest UNVERIFIED), its own table and tests, its own build-time measurement; the thread is shared. Priced at one phase.

### Mating Pair

- **PAIR-06**: The printed test also drives a nominal printed bolt into a bought nut; if it binds, a bolt-side `undersize` field (default 0) becomes a requirement (PAIR-07 below). Moved from v1: deferred by owner ruling 2026-10-22 (06 R9): bought-nut test dropped from Phase 6.
- **PAIR-07**: Bolt-side `undersize` field (default 0) — only if PAIR-06's bought-nut test binds. Deferred with PAIR-06 (06 R9, 2026-10-22).

### Tables and UX

- **TABL-08**: Legacy DIN names (933, 931, 934, 912) resolve to the ISO preset with the wrench-size notice; aliases only, no DIN tables. Trigger: the first user searching by DIN number.
- **INFO-06**: Non-binding print-hint text (orientation, layer height vs pitch). Trigger: the first printed test recorded. Trigger fired: run 06-print-run-1 recorded (2026-10-23); placing it is the owner's roadmap call.

## Out of Scope

Explicitly excluded. Documented to prevent scope creep.

| Feature | Reason |
|---------|--------|
| Self-tapping, wood, sheet-metal screws | Different thread form (sharp, tapered, no mating nut): a separate geometry problem with nothing to prove a pair against. Not deferred — out. |
| Head markings (strength grade, manufacturer) | Printed plastic has no strength grade; text in the kernel means fonts, a separate problem. |
| UNC/UNF and any non-ISO thread form | One thread form to prove; imperial adds tables without adding proof. |
| Fine pitch (ISO 8765/8676/8673 families) | Explicit non-goal for v1: a user-set pitch without an ISO row contradicts the cited-row rule. Revisit as its own standards family. |
| Countersunk screws, set screws, washers | Not in the first two releases; revisit once socket cap has shipped on the proven path. |
| Modelling 6g/6H tolerance classes as geometry | Contradicts "explicit millimetres are truth" and the clearance field; limits are reported numbers only. |
| Sizes below M2 or above M20 | M1.6 does not print; M24+ is long thread builds against the timeout; every row is a test. Range grows when someone needs it. |
| An `unthreaded` / cosmetic-thread flag | Cosmetic bodies are not the product and cannot be proven to mate. A simplified STEP for CAD assemblies is a `docs/ideas/` candidate if CAD users ask. |
| Property class / strength-grade selector, torque and preload charts | Any such number would be a plausible figure nobody can stand behind (L02). |
| Separate DIN 933/931/934/912 tables | Withdrawn standards; doubling every table doubles row liability. Aliases only (TABL-08). |
| Pair check as an HTTP endpoint | 1.6–8 s on a short engaged piece, 4–121 s on full bodies; would consume the admission slot. Offline (tests + CLI) by decision. |
| Server-side accounts or saved designs | The URL is the store; nothing is persisted. |
| Tap-drill / clearance-hole calculators, hole patterns | A second standards family (ISO 273 etc.) with nothing to do with proving a pair. `docs/ideas/` if wanted. |
| Print-in-place, split-print, captive-nut variants | Orthogonal geometry modes. `docs/ideas/`. |
| Extracting the shared infrastructure into a package | Deferred until a fix must land in both repos (L07, `docs/tech_debt/active/2026-10-05-shared-infra-extraction.md`). |
